**Finding: compliant (at fallback).**

- **Customer convenience right** — §17(b) (p0118): Sparkling may terminate "at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice," an unconditional election within the fallback 60–90 day band.
- **No early-termination fee** — no penalty or exit charge appears in §17 or the Fee Schedule references, so the fallback three-month cap is satisfied by absence.
- **Vendor convenience right** — none. Garman may terminate only under §17(c) for insolvency events or uncured material default, and §17(a) makes the term perpetual while fees are paid. This is better than both the fallback (end-of-term, 90 days) and preferred.
- Noted, not redlined: 90 days rather than 30, and no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on our convenience termination. Section 10's renewable one-year maintenance term is a renewal matter, not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so it is not flagged here.
